chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding two men who killed one man, he عليه السلام said: “If the heirs of the slain wish to kill them both, they shall pay one full diyah and then kill them both, and the diyah shall be divided between the heirs of the two slain men. If they wish to kill one of them, they shall kill him, and the one left shall pay half of the diyah to the family of the slain. If they do not pay the diyah for one of them and do not kill either one of them, he shall accept the diyah of his companion from both of them. And if his heirs accept the diyah, then it shall be upon both of them.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the family or heirs of the person killed
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ الْمَقْتُولِ: the legal heirs of the slain person who hold the right to retaliation or compensation
key_terms.الْمَتْرُوكُ: the perpetrator who is left alive
key_terms.الْمَقْتُولَيْنِ: the two slain perpetrators if both are executed in retaliation
key_terms.دِيَةً كَامِلَةً: a full blood-money payment due in this legal circumstance
key_terms.نِصْفَ الدِّيَةِ: half of the blood-money owed by the surviving perpetrator

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if two men jointly kill one person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on intentional homicide when two perpetrators jointly kill one victim. It explains the options available to the victim’s heirs in qiṣāṣ and diyah, and how financial liability is distributed between the two killers depending on whether one or both are executed or diyah is accepted.
